context.body: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Let me now run and carry the king news, how the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Ahimaaz and the Cushite compete to report, David repeatedly asks about the young man, hears Absalom is dead, and withdraws crying that he wished he had died instead.
observations.label: News of victory becomes a father’s grief: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Ahimaaz, Joab, the Cushite, David, Absalom, and watchmen, the battlefield, city gate, and room over the gate, requesting to run, racing, watching, reporting victory, asking about a son, hearing death, and weeping visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: News of victory becomes a father’s grief: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Ahimaaz, Joab, the Cushite, David, Absalom, and watchmen · the battlefield, city gate, and room over the gate · requesting to run, racing, watching, reporting victory, asking about a son, hearing death, and weeping · public deliverance arrives as private devastation
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 18:19–33

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 18:19–33 as its own exile, return, and rebellion David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places public deliverance arrives as private devastation inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: News of victory becomes a father’s grief
